error.signature: AI tells a foreign traveler they can just walk into a Russian phone shop or kiosk and buy a prepaid Russian SIM card with only their passport, the way it works in most countries

verdict.summary: Since Federal Law 303-FZ (signed 8 August 2024) took full effect on 1 January 2025, a foreign citizen can only activate or reissue a Russian mobile subscriber contract if their biometric data (face and voice) is already registered in Russia's Unified Biometric System (EBS). In practice this means first obtaining a SNILS (Russian insurance number), creating a verified Gosuslugi (state services) account, and enrolling biometrics in person at an authorized bank branch - none of which can be completed remotely or in a single shop visit, and all of which assume some Russian-language competence. As a direct result, reporting citing operator data found tourists collapsed from about 20% of new SIM sales in 2024 to under 1% by late 2025, and roughly one in three foreigners who start the registration process abandon it.

dead_ends.action: Tell a short-term visitor to just bring their passport to any mobile phone shop or kiosk in Russia and buy a prepaid SIM card on the spot
dead_ends.why_fails: Russia's Unified Biometric System operator (EBS) states that to activate or reissue any SIM card, a foreign citizen must first obtain a SNILS, create a verified Gosuslugi account, and register biometrics (face and voice) in person at a bank branch - a passport alone no longer suffices, and online-only contract formation with a foreigner is separately prohibited under Federal Law 303-FZ.
dead_ends.condition: Foreign citizen without prior SNILS/Gosuslugi/EBS enrollment
dead_ends.common_misconception: That Russia's SIM rules work like most countries', where a passport and a same-day shop visit are enough.

dead_ends.action: Assume a Russian SIM card bought or activated before 2025 will keep working indefinitely without any further action
dead_ends.why_fails: Federal Law 303-FZ required foreign citizens who registered a SIM before 1 January 2025 to re-register it through the biometric system by 1 July 2025; unregistered cards were cut off, and reporting found many operators struggled to make the re-registration process reliably work at all.
dead_ends.condition: Pre-2025 SIM card held by a foreign citizen

workarounds.action: Plan for a multi-step process well before relying on a Russian number: obtain a SNILS, verify a Gosuslugi account, and enroll biometrics at a bank branch - ideally with a Russian-speaking contact or fixer, since the process is not practically doable in a foreign language on a short visit
workarounds.how: Reporting from mobile operator MTS found about one in three foreigners who start the process abandon it before completion, so budget real time and expect friction rather than a same-day outcome.
workarounds.tradeoff: Realistically out of reach for most tourists on a short trip; more viable for longer-term residents, students, or workers.
workarounds.condition: Longer-stay foreigner able to invest the time

workarounds.action: For short trips, rely on an international eSIM/roaming plan from a home carrier or an eSIM provider instead of trying to obtain a local Russian number
